writerFeedback:
The draft reads with a confident, analyst-style voice and moves logically from portfolio-level performance into specific holdings, which gives the reader a clear sense of what is driving results. The holding-level color on St. Pancras, Fortysouth, and Affinity Water adds useful texture rather than just restating headline numbers.

The weakness is repetition and density as a pattern: EBITDA growth and "across the portfolio" phrasing recur in back-to-back sentences, and several paragraphs stack multiple ideas (operations, commercial, refinancing) without a connective thread, which flattens emphasis. Watch also for small consistency issues like the HICL/HCIL spelling and clarify whether items such as the refinancing refer to the company or to a specific holding, since the antecedents drift.

sentences.text: HICL Infrastructure’s performance for the five months to 28 February 2026 was positive and largely in line with expectations.

note.text: The source describes operational performance as "in line with expectations" and "robust" over the period 1 October 2025 to 28 February 2026. The statement's "positive and largely in line with expectations" restates the same assertion in other words.

sentences.text: Meanwhile, Affinity Water appointed a new CEO with significant sector experience and stands to benefit from the UK government’s recently published white paper on water sector reform.

occurrences.extract: | · | £50m of the sale proceeds was allocated to fund HICL's equity commitment to Affinity Water, as previously disclosed. Proceeds of c.£66m will be allocated to funding the existing equity commitments to Blankenburg tunnel and B247, due in September and December 2026 respectively, also as previously disclosed. This contribution meets HICL's deferred equity obligations as these assets successfully complete construction and move into their operational phase. |

| · | o  At Affinity Water, the management team remains focused on delivering the AMP8 business plan. During the period, the company appointed Mark Garth as Chief Executive Officer, who brings significant sector experience from United Utilities particularly in relation to achieving industry-leading operational performance. HICL continues to expect distributions from Affinity Water ahead of 31 March 2026. The Company notes the publication of the UK Government white paper on water sector reform, which is largely consistent with the final recommendations of the Cunliffe Report, many of which are expected to be beneficial for strong performers such as Affinity Water. |

Over the same period, overall movement in bond yields in the United States, Canada, New Zealand and the Eurozone has been relatively flat. Transaction activity in the period, including direct experience from HICL's recent disposals and InfraRed's broader platform, reinforces the Investment Manager's view that there is no strong evidence to support a movement in discount rates.
